Rafael Nadal. A Spanish tennis icon who won twenty-two Grand Slam singles titles, surpassing Roger Federer's previous record as the greatest in tennis history. Renowned for his clay-court dominance and powerful topspin game, Nadal's fourteen French Open titles are unmatched by any player at a single tournament, and his relentless competitiveness defines the modern era. He won fourteen French Opens spanning from 2005 through 2006, 2007 through 2009, 2010 through 2014, 2017 through 2018, and 2019 through 2022. He also won four US Opens, two Wimbledons, and two Australian Opens across his distinguished career. His fourteen French Open titles represent the most by any player at a single Grand Slam tournament, and his clay-court dominance across multiple decades is historically unparalleled. Known for his aggressive topspin forehand, muscular physique, and distinctive sleeveless shirts and tight shorts, his intensity and never-say-die attitude are iconic in the sport. He reached world number one in 2008 and held it for 209 weeks, with his peak years from 2008 to 2013 overlapping with both Federer and Djokovic, creating the memorable "Big Three" era. He competed at the Olympics and won gold medals in both singles and doubles. He continued competing at the highest levels into his late thirties, retiring in 2024 after sustained success across three full decades of professional tennis.
